decisions.decision: Fixed resolve_port_identity() in control/detect_devices.py to use a genuine read-only calibration comparison (bus.read_calibration() vs the id's saved file) instead of a write_calibration()-based no-op-succeeds test.
decisions.rationale: Live testing before this session found the original write-based test could silently 'confirm' a wrong robot id with zero real signal, when the id/class combination resolves to no saved calibration file (write_calibration({}) is a no-op that never raises). Verified no hardware corruption occurred by that bug (follower's live servo values still matched its saved file exactly) before applying the fix. Commit eb85f22 in the phase-11 worktree (worktree-agent-afe9e290a91f86d2e).

decisions.decision: Switched StereoSplitCamera's AR0144 capture backend from cv2.VideoCapture to an ffmpeg subprocess, and switched device_map.json's stereo camera identifier from a numeric cv2/ffmpeg index to the AVFoundation device NAME string ('CCB Camera').
decisions.rationale: cv2.VideoCapture's AVFoundation backend cannot be made to report the AR0144's true 2560x720 frame on macOS (confirmed unfixed OpenCV bug, opencv/opencv#23368) -- it silently serves a lower resolution regardless of explicit CAP_PROP requests. ffmpeg with explicit -pixel_format uyvy422 -video_size 2560x720 captures the real frame reliably. Separately found that ffmpeg's OWN AVFoundation device index numbering is not stable between process launches (same physical camera showed up at a different index moments apart), so device_map.json now persists cameras.stereo_overhead_name (the device name) as the authoritative identifier for the ffmpeg path, keeping the numeric cameras.stereo_overhead only for the unrelated, non-safety-critical IOLogger cv2 recording caps. Commit 0541458.

decisions.decision: Fixed detect_devices() to default the leader identity check to _make_leader_robot (SOLeader) instead of silently falling back to _make_follower_robot.
decisions.rationale: main() never passed make_leader through to detect_devices(), so the leader check always constructed an SO101Follower even for the leader id -- whose calibration_fpath resolves under robots/so_follower/, where the leader's real saved calibration never lives (it's under teleoperators/so_leader/). Leader auto-discovery was dead on arrival since Task 2 landed; only surfaced now because this session re-tested with the leader physically connected and powered. Commit e8519f8.
